newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Arabs ask U.N. council to halt Israeli construction.
newsitem.headline: Arabs ask U.N. council to halt Israeli construction.

text.p: The Arab group asked on Wednesday for an immediate meeting of the Security Council to adopt a resolution calling on Israel to halt a controversial construction project in Arab East Jerusalem, Arab sources said.
They said the request was submitted to council president Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland by ambassador Nasser al-Khalifa of Qatar, current chairman of the 22-member group.
The council might meet on Thursday, the sources said.
The Arab group's request was similar to one submitted late on Tuesday by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa.

This followed the start of work by Israel on the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews on a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem which Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. The site is called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians and Har Homa by Israelis.

The sources said the Arab group would submit a resolution calling for the work to be halted, though there was considerable speculation the United States would again use its veto, as it did on March 7, to block a resolution calling on Israel to abandon its construction plans.

The new resolution would be simpler and more direct than the earlier, vetoed draft that was sponsored by the council's four European Union members -- Britain, France, Portugal and Sweden -- the sources said.

After the U.S. veto, almost the same resolution was adopted on March 13 by the General Assembly by a vote of 130 to 2, with two abstentions. The United States and Israel cast the only negative votes. There is no veto in the 185-nation Assembly, whose decisions are not binding.

The United States, like virtually all other speakers in both the Assembly and council debates, criticised Israel's decision but said the United Nations was not the appropriate forum for dealing with issues that should be settled bilaterally between Israel and the Palestinians.
